title: Block editor labels written as AngularJS templates
description: Block List and Block Grid block labels configured for the AngularJS backoffice, such as {{ title }} or {{ text | ncRichText | truncate:true:36 }}. They live in the data type configuration in the database, and in serialized configuration files when a synchronization package or a deployment tool is used.

impact.summary: The AngularJS backoffice is removed and block labels are rendered with Umbraco Flavored Markdown. Labels written as AngularJS templates must be rewritten: on a 13.10.1 to 17.8.1 upgrade the migrations left them unchanged and the backoffice showed the template as raw text in the block and in the block editor title.

sources.evidence: With the removal of AngularJS, advanced label rendering is now handled using Umbraco Flavored Markdown
With the removal of AngularJS, advanced label rendering is now handled using Umbraco Flavored Markdown

handling.option: Rewrite each label in Umbraco Flavored Markdown after the database migration, keeping the text around the template: {{ alias }} becomes {umbValue: alias}, the ncRichText filter becomes stripHtml, and truncate:true:N becomes truncate:N. Do it in the backoffice of every environment after its upgrade, or in the serialized files the environments import, so an import does not bring the old labels back.
handling.when: Test-DatabaseHealth.ps1 lists blockLabelTemplates on the local copy, or discovery found labels with {{ }} in serialized configuration files
